item.title: A comprehensive global ocean radiocarbon dataset (1700–2024) for climate applications
item.description:
A comprehensive global ocean radiocarbon dataset (1700–2024) for climate applications
Nabir Mamnun, Branwen Williams, Rena Mukherjee, Roberta L. Hansman, Rolf Sonnerup, Nikita Tournebise, Tim DeVries, and Heather Graven
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8949–8969, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8949-2026, 2026
Radiocarbon measurements in the ocean are key to studying ocean circulation, gas exchange and the carbon cycle, but they are sparse and scattered across many sources. We combined about 68,500 measurements from ship-based seawater samples (1955–2024) and biogenic carbonates (corals and shells, 1700–2020) into one quality-checked, openly available dataset. The dataset provides the most comprehensive record of ocean radiocarbon over the industrial period, including impacts of nuclear bomb tests.

item.title: OMNIE-Nutrients: A Global Gridded Ocean Nutrient Dataset (1965–2022) Derived from a Neural Network Emulator and In-Situ Observations
item.description:
OMNIE-Nutrients: A Global Gridded Ocean Nutrient Dataset (1965–2022) Derived from a Neural Network Emulator and In-Situ Observations
Said Ouala and Zouhair Lachkar
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-714,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
OMNIE-Nutrients is a global gridded dataset of marine macronutrients (nitrate, phosphate, silicate) spanning 1965–2022. It integrates sparse in situ observations with machine-learning-emulated profiles derived from hydrographic data, expanding the effective observational network by an order of magnitude. These interpolated fields eliminate severe artifacts and historical sampling biases prevalent in standard climatologies, providing a robust baseline for evaluating biogeochemical variability.

item.title: SeismicX-Cont: a coverage-aware continuous seismic data product for operational earthquake monitoring
item.description:
SeismicX-Cont: a coverage-aware continuous seismic data product for operational earthquake monitoring
Ziye Yu, Xin Liu, Yuqi Cai, Yanru An, Fajun Miao, Tengchao Dong, and Tingting Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-753,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Earthquake monitoring needs continuous recordings, including periods with missing data and signals absent from existing catalogues. SeismicX-Cont links two weeks of California recordings with station availability, earthquake annotations and instrument information. It lets users distinguish unavailable input from missed arrivals and repeat evaluations on shared data. The release includes validation tools and a small example dataset.

item.title: Ocean surface wave advanced parameters from the SWIM instrument on board CFOSAT
item.description:
Ocean surface wave advanced parameters from the SWIM instrument on board CFOSAT
Jérôme Lebreton, Matthias Averseng, Charles Peureux, Danièle Hauser, Lotfi Aouf, Cédric Tourain, and Annabelle Olivier
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-928,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Ocean waves play a key role in exchanges between the ocean and the atmosphere and can pose risks to maritime activities. Using observations from the Franco-Chinese CFOSAT satellite, we have created a new dataset describing wave characteristics, their structure and indicators of potentially dangerous sea conditions. This dataset makes satellite observations easier to use and contributes to a better understanding of ocean conditions, particularly during extreme events.

item.title: Developing a spatially distributed typical meteorological year dataset for solar radiation assessment in Australia
item.description:
Developing a spatially distributed typical meteorological year dataset for solar radiation assessment in Australia
Jingpeng Fu, Pingan Ni, Deo Prasad, Guojin Qin, Fuming Lei, Yingjun Yue, Jiaqing Yan, Zengfeng Yan, and Bao-Jie He
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8923–8947, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8923-2026, 2026
This study created a new set of recent weather files for 353 locations across Australia to support solar energy and building design. Using NASA weather records from 2009 to 2023, we compared sunlight patterns with an existing reference product and adjusted the results for clear and cloudy conditions. The data matched well on clear days, while cloudy days showed larger differences. The work can help planners, engineers, and researchers assess solar potential where local measurements are limited.

item.title: Overview of ParallelClim-WestUS-Daily – high-resolution observed and counterfactual daily climate data for the western United States, 1951–2025
item.description:
Overview of ParallelClim-WestUS-Daily – high-resolution observed and counterfactual daily climate data for the western United States, 1951–2025
A. Park Williams, John T. Abatzoglou, Gavin D. Madakumbura, Haibo Liu, Stefan Rahimi, and Christopher Daly
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8865–8901, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8865-2026, 2026
Here we introduce ParallelClim-WestUS-Daily, a new dataset of daily gridded climate data for the western US from 1951–2025 as well as a parallel, counterfactual realization of the observed climate without human-caused climate change. This dataset will enable assessments of how climate change has affected complex hydroclimatic processes such as hydrology, vegetation dynamics, and wildfire.

item.title: High-resolution BIOCLIM and ENVIREM grids for Europe in the last 21,000 years: downscaled CCSM3 simulations compared to pollen-based reconstructions
item.description:
High-resolution BIOCLIM and ENVIREM grids for Europe in the last 21,000 years: downscaled CCSM3 simulations compared to pollen-based reconstructions
Jan Divíšek, Michal Hájek, Michal Horsák, and Petra Hájková
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-502,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Understanding past climate change helps us predict future impacts on biodiversity. We developed a detailed climate dataset for Europe covering the last 21,000 years in 100-year steps. After validating the data against alternative models and fossil-pollen reconstructions, we provide a reliable, open-access tool that enables researchers to accurately simulate and track how species respond to changing climates.

item.title: GIFT-BDS: a high-resolution TEC and Gradient Ionospheric Index dataset over China derived from BeiDou GEO fixed-geometry observations
item.description:
GIFT-BDS: a high-resolution TEC and Gradient Ionospheric Index dataset over China derived from BeiDou GEO fixed-geometry observations
Zhiyao Li, Jiahao Zhong, Ningbo Wang, Yongqiang Hao, Yunbin Yuan, Norbert Jakowski, Mohammed Mainul Hoque, Ang Liu, Zishen Li, and Xin Wan
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8903–8921, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8903-2026, 2026
We provide a high-resolution dataset describing spatiotemporal variability in the ionized upper atmosphere over China at finer spatial resolution than conventional global products. It is produced from a ground-based receiver network and geostationary navigation satellites using fixed-geometry observations to resolve spatial gradients. The dataset supports studies of upper-atmosphere coupling within the Earth system and assessment of space-weather impacts on satellite positioning accuracy.

item.title: The Improvement of the reconstruction of OHC based on DINCAE
item.description:
The Improvement of the reconstruction of OHC based on DINCAE
Tao Xie, Wenying Mao, Hengqian Yan, Mei Hong, Jian Li, Wenmei Li, Yixiang Chen, Yi Huang, Xiaobo Zhu, and Haili Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-617,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Ocean absorbs >93 % of excess global warming heat, making heat content a key metric. Sparse observations limit tracking. We use DINCAE deep-learning to reconstruct 1960–2024 ocean temps from quality profiles. Reconstruction matches independent data, capturing warming, seasons, and ENSO. Heat uptake rate agrees with satellite energy imbalance, confirming reliability. Data public.

item.title: High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
item.description:
High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
Süleyman Selim Çallı, Kübra Özdemir Çallı, Brahim Akdim, Bruno Arfib, Vincent Bailly-Comte, Aleksey Benderev, Sandra Béranger, Avi Burg, Onur Can, Jean-Baptiste Charlier, Mehmet Çelik, Arda Melih Çetin, Fehdi Chemseddine, Huan Fang Dang, Miroslava Deliyska, Lucio Di Matteo, Marco Dionigi, Virgil Dragusin, Romeo Eftimi, Jutta Eybl, Davide Fronzi, Nico Goldscheider, Ergin Gökkaya, István Gabor Hatvani, Jorge Jódar, Hervé Jourde, Eva Kaminsky, Konstantina Katsanou, Alireza Kavousi, Melike Kaya, Zoltán Kern, David Labat, Bernard Ladouche, Tanja Liesch, Peter Malík, Jean-Christophe Maréchal, Christian Massari, Cyril Mayaud, Naomi Mazzilli, Pavel Pracný, Nataša Ravbar, Nathan Rispal, Simon Seelig, Vianney Sivelle, Marc Steinmann, Daniela Valigi, Gerfried Winkler, Ahmet K. Yahşi, Eleni Zagana, Yining Zang, and Andreas Hartmann
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8841–8864, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8841-2026, 2026
Karst groundwater systems are vital but highly sensitive to climate change. Their complex underground flow makes them hard to manage without good data, so we gathered 129 high-quality records of spring discharge across Mediterranean mountain ranges. With an average of 21 years of data – including one nearly century-long record – this collection provides the detailed information needed to better predict water availability and protect these vulnerable groundwater sources.

item.title: The consistent in-situ global gridded temperature and salinity dataset, CORA OA 1960–2024
item.description:
The consistent in-situ global gridded temperature and salinity dataset, CORA OA 1960–2024
Tanguy Szekely and Jean-Renaud Miadana
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8821–8840, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8821-2026, 2026
The ocean stores vast amounts of heat and plays a central role in regulating Earth's climate. Monitoring its temperature and salinity is essential to understand climate change. We present an updated global ocean dataset covering the past six decades, built by combining historical measurements from ships, floats, and buoys. The dataset is freely available and regularly updated, providing scientists with a reliable reference for climate studies, ocean modeling, and satellite data verification.
